entries.title: Docs Studio (beta): build and host a docs site for your product
entries.summary: Write documentation in the browser, pick a theme, and publish a fast docs site with search and Ask AI. Free while it's in beta.
entries.body:
- **Create a site** in a workspace or on your own, blank or from a template (product docs, API reference, help center), at a free `<name>.docs.markdrop.in` address.
- **Import from GitBook:** pages, images, navigation, icons, brand and old links come across, with a report of what needs a look before you publish.
- **A visual editor** with a slash menu for callouts, steps, tabs, cards, code and images with dark versions, or plain Markdown. Drafts save as you type, every save is a version, and one person edits a page at a time.
- **Six themes** (Clean, Editorial, Technical, Minimal, Playful, Help center), your logo and colours with checked contrast, fonts, corners, colour mode and custom CSS.
- **Publish** when you're ready: see what changed, follow the build, and put an earlier publish back in seconds. Turn on reviews to have changes approved first.
- **Docs Studio roles** (Admin, Reviewer, Editor, Viewer), separate from workspace roles, with per-site roles and a history of changes.
- **For readers:** search, Ask AI with sources, light and dark, and a Markdown copy of every page, `llms.txt` and an MCP server for AI tools.
- Coming soon: your own domain, password-protected and members-only sites, and GitHub sync.

entries.title: CLI 0.5.1: install fix, Windows on Arm, sends listed under your account
entries.summary: The one-line installer no longer prints an error, Windows on Arm gets a working build, and send and the local MCP server use the token saved by markdrop login.
entries.body:
- The install script for macOS and Linux started with stray characters, so `curl … | sh` printed a "not found" error before installing. It now runs cleanly.
- On Windows on Arm, the PowerShell installer installs the x64 build, which runs under emulation, instead of failing.
- `markdrop send` and the local MCP server now use the token saved by `markdrop login` when `MARKDROP_TOKEN` isn't set, so your shares appear in your account. `send` also takes `--token`.
- `markdrop mcp --help` lists all eleven tools, and `markdrop upload` on a folder explains how to publish a website or send the folder instead.

entries.title: Restore old file versions, transfer a workspace, and leave what's shared with you
entries.summary: A file's Settings lists its versions to restore or delete, workspace owners can hand over ownership, and people added to a document or file can remove themselves.
entries.body:
- **Versions:** a file's **Settings** lists its last five versions. Restore one to make it current again at the same link, or delete an old one to free space.
- **Transfer ownership:** a workspace owner can make another member the owner from the **People** tab, and becomes an admin.
- **Remove me:** people added to a document or file can take themselves off it from **Shared with me** or the item's menu.
- **New edit secret:** the owner of a document can replace a leaked edit secret from **Document settings**.
- **Fixes:** the keyboard-shortcuts setting now turns off F and /, admin-only workspace controls say "Admins only" consistently, and zipped sites no longer count skipped files towards their limits.

entries.title: Send API requests from the docs, and see each feature
entries.summary: Try it on every API page now calls the live API, and the guides have screenshots in light and dark, short clips and narrated videos.
entries.body:
- **Try it sends the request.** Fill in the form on an endpoint page and choose **Send request** to call the live API from your browser. You see the status, the time it took, the headers and the body. Requests that create, change or delete something ask you to confirm first, and a document published from Try it expires after a day.
- **Screenshots, clips and videos** across the guides, from publishing and sharing to workspaces, analytics, Send and the AI pages. Screenshots follow your light or dark theme; click one to enlarge it.
- **A new changelog.** Search, filter by product, and see what changed since the CLI version you have.
highlights: Try it calls the live API

entries.title: Workspace header, account menu and title fixes
entries.summary: Pages on a workspace's own domain show its logo and name together, account menus open over the document bar, and a document that starts with its own title no longer shows it twice.
entries.body:
- On a workspace's own domain, the top bar shows the workspace logo next to its name, lined up with the rest of the page. A wide logo that already contains the name is shown on its own.
- The account menu in the top bar opened behind the document's toolbar. It now opens on top, on markdrop.in and on workspace domains.
- A document whose Markdown starts with its own main heading shows only that heading, even when it differs from the document's title. The title still names the page in the top bar, the browser tab and link previews.
- Publishing a password-protected document while signed in could leave the page loading forever. It now opens the Published panel with your links.
- Parts of a document's page that load when you first use them, like the share dialog, no longer flash the full-page loader.

entries.title: Docs with Ask AI
entries.summary: docs.markdrop.in: every guide, an API reference, and an assistant that answers from the docs with links to the exact section.
entries.body:
Markdrop now has documentation at **docs.markdrop.in**.

- **Ask AI** answers from these docs, cites the exact section for each point, and highlights it when you open the source.
- **API reference** for every public endpoint, with curl, JavaScript, Python and CLI examples and a Try it form that builds the command for you.
- **For your AI app:** every page has a Markdown version, the whole site is in `/llms.txt`, and a docs MCP server lets Claude, Cursor or VS Code search the docs as you work.
- **Copy page** and **Open in Claude or ChatGPT** on every page, and a mark on sections that changed since your last visit.
highlights: Answers link to the exact section

entries.title: Creator analytics
entries.summary: See how each document, PDF, video and audio file you publish is read or watched, live and over time.
entries.body:
Every document and file you own now has its own analytics page, and **Analytics** in your dashboard shows them all together.

- **Video and audio:** how many people are still watching at 0:30, 25%, 50%, 75% and the end, where most of them leave, and how playback went.
- **Markdown documents:** how many read to the end, how far readers get section by section, and what they copy and which links they click.
- **PDFs:** how many readers reach each page.
- **Live now:** who is reading or watching right now.

Your own views are never counted, and you can download a document's numbers as CSV. AI apps connected to Markdrop can ask for the same numbers with the new `get_document_analytics` tool.

entries.title: Light is the default theme
entries.summary: Markdrop now opens in the light theme unless you choose dark or system.
entries.body: New visitors see Markdrop in the light theme. Your choice is remembered per browser: pick dark, or system to follow your device, from the theme switch.

entries.title: Simpler workspaces
entries.summary: One sidebar for your files and workspaces, folders you can drop files onto, and sharing in one dialog.
entries.body:
Workspaces were redesigned around one drive-style sidebar: **My files**, **Shared with me**, **Recent** and each workspace's folder tree.

- **Folder view** shows who can open what in a folder at a glance, and you can drop files onto it to upload them.
- **Preview as** shows a workspace the way someone else would see it.
- **One share dialog** with three presets: *Only people added*, *{Workspace} team* and *Anyone with the link*. Passwords and expiry are under **More options**, for documents too.
- **Request access:** people who can't open a document can ask for access, and you decide from an email or the app.
- **Search** with :kbd[⌘K] across your documents, files and folders.

Documents and files now open in a new tab, at the address **Copy link** gives you, on your workspace's own domain when it has one.

entries.title: Passwords and expiry from the share dialog
entries.summary: Set or remove a document's password and expiry from the share dialog, including a new one-hour expiry.
entries.body:
The share dialog's **More options** now sets a password and an expiry for Markdown documents as well as files, including **On a date…**, and the new one-hour option. The dialog also shows the document's real address.

For scripts, `PATCH /api/v1/documents/{slug}/settings` changes the password and expiry without resending the content.

A document published without a title now takes one from its first heading or first line.

entries.title: Workspaces, folders and custom domains, rebuilt
entries.summary: Share whole folders, keep one access level per document at every address, and run your workspace on your own domain more safely.
entries.body:
Workspaces, folders and custom domains were rebuilt on one access rule: a document has one access level at every address it has, on markdrop.in and on your workspace's domain alike.

- **Share a folder** with a single link. People see only the items they can already open.
- **Renamed addresses** send readers to the new one, and old addresses are never handed to someone else.
- **Custom domains** are re-checked every day. A domain whose DNS no longer points at Markdrop stops serving after three days of failed checks.
- **Editors and workspace members** can replace a file from the viewer.
- **AI apps** can list workspaces and folders, file documents, create folders and move items, and the CLI can upload straight into a folder.

Existing workspace links keep working.

entries.title: CLI 0.5.0: publish into workspaces
entries.summary: Upload straight into a workspace folder, choose the address, and list your workspaces from the terminal.
entries.body:
```bash
markdrop workspaces                     # your workspaces, roles and live domains
markdrop workspaces Acme                # its folders
markdrop upload spec.pdf --workspace Acme --folder guides/setup
markdrop upload demo.mp4 --slug q3-demo
```

- `--workspace` takes a workspace's id, name or custom domain; `--folder` an existing folder path.
- The printed link is on the workspace's custom domain when it has a live one.
- `--slug` picks the address and fails before uploading if it is taken.
- `markdrop mcp` gains `list_workspaces` and `list_folders`, and its `upload_file` takes `workspace`, `folder` and `slug`.

On the hosted MCP server, seven workspace tools arrived at the same time: `list_workspaces`, `list_folders`, `list_workspace_items`, `add_to_workspace`, `remove_from_workspace`, `create_folder` and `move_to_folder`.

entries.title: Replace a file and keep its link
entries.summary: Swap the video, PDF or page behind a link you already shared, keep the last five versions, and publish videos up to 2 GB.
entries.body:
Re-recorded the demo? Revised the PDF? Replace the file and everyone with the link gets the new one. The link, its access, title and view count stay the same.

- **Versions:** the last five versions of each file are kept, and you can restore any of them. A restore is itself a new version, so nothing is lost.
- **Bigger files:** video and audio up to 2 GB each, sent in parts and checked by SHA-256 before they go live. Storage is 20 GB per account, earlier versions included.
- **Audio files** (MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG) get their own player, and videos show a poster frame before they play.
- **From anywhere:** replace a file on markdrop.in, with `markdrop replace`, or from an AI app.
highlights: Video and audio up to 2 GB

entries.title: CLI 0.4.0: upload, replace and versions
entries.summary: Publish files from the terminal and swap them behind the same link, with resumable uploads and JSON output for scripts.
entries.body:
New commands: `upload`, `replace`, `versions`, `restore`, `info`, `login` and `logout`.

- Uploads are hashed, sent four parts at a time, verified by Markdrop, and resume when you run the same command again.
- `--json` prints one JSON object and nothing else, for scripts and CI.
- `markdrop login` saves an API token so you don't need `MARKDROP_TOKEN` in every shell.
- `markdrop mcp` gains `upload_file`, `replace_file`, `list_file_versions`, `restore_file_version` and `get_file_info`, so an AI app on your computer can publish files from disk.

entries.title: Replacing a video over 25 MB works again
entries.summary: Replacing a video file used the 25 MB limit for documents and refused larger videos.
entries.body: Replacing the file behind a video link now uses the video size limit, and checks your storage with the old file counted as freed.

entries.title: Send files from an AI app on your computer
entries.summary: markdrop mcp, a local MCP server in the CLI, lets Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code share and receive files peer to peer.
entries.body:
Add `markdrop mcp` to an AI app on your computer and ask it to "share these three PDFs" or "download this share link into ~/Projects".

- `share_files`, `share_status`, `stop_share` and `receive_share` run on your machine; files go straight to the recipient.
- Well-known secret locations such as `~/.ssh` and `.env` files are refused.
- `markdrop send` and `get` now use a relay when a direct connection between networks isn't possible.
- On the hosted server, `list_shares` and `get_share_status` show your shares and check a share link.

entries.title: Connect Claude, ChatGPT and other AI apps
entries.summary: Markdrop's MCP server lets your AI assistant publish, read and update your documents, after you approve it on Markdrop.
entries.body:
Paste `https://api.markdrop.in/mcp` into Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or another MCP app, sign in to Markdrop and approve. There's no key to copy.

- Ask for "a Markdrop doc of these notes" and get a link that renders.
- Publish HTML pages, read and update documents, change who can open them, and see how they're read.
- Two permissions, *Read your documents* and *Publish and change documents*, approved per app.
- Disconnect any app from **Settings → Connected apps**.

Assistants can't read end-to-end encrypted documents or get past a password.

entries.title: Peer-to-peer shares survive a dropped connection
entries.summary: A sender whose connection drops takes their link back, recipients wait for them, and transfers between different networks go through a relay.
entries.body:
- A sender whose browser reconnects takes its share link back instead of being locked out of it.
- Recipients who open the link while the sender is away wait up to 10 minutes for them to return.
- When the two computers can't connect directly, the transfer goes through a relay. The relay can't read the encrypted connection.

entries.title: Large HTML files publish from VS Code
entries.summary: HTML and other text files up to 25 MB now publish and sync from VS Code; larger self-contained pages used to fail.
entries.body: Self-contained HTML pages with inlined images or fonts between 10 and 25 MB failed to publish from VS Code. The limit for files synced from the editor is now 25 MB, the same as for uploads.

entries.title: Privacy page and privacy choices
entries.summary: A privacy page explains what Markdrop collects, and visitors from the EU, EEA, UK and Switzerland choose whether to allow analytics.
entries.body:
- The new [privacy page](https://markdrop.in/privacy) explains what Markdrop collects and why.
- Visitors from the EU, EEA, UK and Switzerland are asked before product analytics run. Declining, or sending Global Privacy Control, keeps analytics from storing anything in your browser.
- **Privacy choices** in the footer reopens the choice at any time.
- Product analytics never see your documents' addresses or what you type.

entries.title: A new Markdrop
entries.summary: Every screen was redesigned on one design system, with a new reader, a new upload page and a light theme.
entries.body:
- A new reader for documents and files, full screen or framed, with clearer messages when a link needs a password or a sign-in.
- A new upload page, editor and publish settings.
- Settings pages for your account, API tokens and workspaces.
- A light theme alongside dark.

entries.title: Send many files to many people from one link
entries.summary: One share link now serves up to 10 recipients at once, carries several files, and shows who is downloading.
entries.body:
- Add several files to one share and send them all with one link.
- Up to 10 people can download from the link at the same time.
- See who is connected and how far along each download is.
- Recipients are told when the sender closes the link.
- Links made in the browser work with `markdrop get`.

entries.title: Share documents with people
entries.summary: Choose who can open a document when you publish it, and add people by email as viewers or editors.
entries.body:
- Pick who can open a document when you create it, and change it later from the document.
- Add people by email with **Can view** or **Can edit**. They sign in to open it.
- Folders in a workspace are part of the address, so a document's link shows where it is filed.

entries.title: Workspaces on your own domain
entries.summary: Create a workspace, invite your team, and serve its documents on your own domain with your branding.
entries.body:
- Workspaces with members and roles, and invitations people accept.
- Serve a workspace's documents on a domain you own, verified through DNS.
- Your logo and accent colour on your domain, and link previews in your brand.
- Video files with their own player.

entries.title: End-to-end encrypted documents
entries.summary: Encrypt a document in your browser so Markdrop stores only ciphertext and the key lives in the link.
entries.body:
Turn on encryption when you publish and the document is encrypted in your browser with AES-256-GCM before it is sent. The key is part of the link after `#k=`, which browsers never send to a server, so Markdrop can't read the document.

Anyone with the full link can read it; anyone without the key part can't, including Markdrop and AI apps.
